Innkeeper. I have something to show you.
Garok draws a beast's bone
from his belt. Notches crowd it.
I said I'd pay the roof debt in steel.
…I cut one notch.
This house's share.
I stood at the door. It did not open.
…I cut one notch.
This house's share.
금 하나에 약속 하나.\n그런데 하나는 반만 그었다.\n끝을 못 맺은 약:
One notch, one promise.
But one I cut only halfway.
A promise I never finished.
인간 일가를 고개 너머로\n데려다주기로 했다.\n그런데 마을 문이 나를:
I swore to guide a human family
over the pass.
The village gate shut when it saw me.
아이가 울었다. 나를 보고.\n…그래서 사흘을 뒤에서 걸었다.\n안 보이:
The child cried. At me.
…So for three days I walked behind.
Out of sight. Far back.
…그 마을 심정, 알 것 같소.\n내 할아버지도 횃불을 받았지.\n오크를:
…I know how that village felt.
My grandfather took a torch too.
They'd bar the door at an orc.
I know. Still, you
keep your blade off the innkeeper.
…That is enough.
A promise kept three days in hiding,
and he calls it half a notch.
You got them all the way there.
…The promise was 'I will guide.'
Not 'I will follow in secret.'
…But your word is my witness.
The other half I cut tonight.
Leave the half notch as it is.
…Yes. Because it is half,
this notch holds on to me.
Cut it whole and I forget.
Orcs do not carve to forget.
We carve to remember.
That child must be grown now.
…Do they still cry at orcs?
그 반 금, 다 그었다.\n주인 말을 증인 삼아.\n…그런데 소식이 왔다:
That half notch, I finished it.
With your word as witness.
…Then word came.
반 금은 그대로 뒀다.\n밤마다 손가락으로 만졌다.\n…그런데 소식이 왔:
I left the half notch as it was.
Touched it every night.
…Then word came.
In Garok's great palm
lies a clumsily carved wooden tusk.
그 집 아이가 보냈다.\n'뒤에서 걷던 오크 아저씨께.'\n…알고 있었다:
The family's child sent it.
'To the orc who walked behind.'
…They knew. From the start.
그거 제가 날랐어요!\n받는 이가 '뒤에서 걷는 오크'라서\n역참 세 군:
I carried that one!
It was for 'the orc who walks behind,'
so I asked at three waystations!
…My thanks, courier.
No orc of my tribe has ever
received a letter. I am the first.
There are letters cut in the tusk.
Not orc letters.
…Innkeeper, read it for me.
삐뚤빼뚤, 꾹꾹 눌러 판 글씨.\n'무서워해서 미안해요.':
Crooked, hard-pressed letters.
'Sorry I was scared of you.'
…오크는 무섭다. 그건 맞다.\n무서워도 미안해하는 아이라.\n…이 금은:
…Orcs are frightening. That is true.
A child scared, and sorry anyway.
…This notch I must cut differently.
Write back. I'll pen it for you.
…An orc writing back to a human child.
The ancestors would laugh.
그래도 쓰자. 짧게.\n'다음엔 앞에서 걷겠다.':
Still, we write. Short.
'Next time I walk in front.'
This tusk hangs beside the bone.
…It is not a promise. It is an answer.
지난번 저녁 내가 냈지?\n토끼 셋! 다들 잘 먹었잖아.\n오늘은 더 커:
Last supper was mine, yes?
Three rabbits! Everyone ate well.
Today's bigger. A deer!
I kept watch all night. As promised!
So I caught one. A deer!
…A big one.
크라냐가 사슴 반쪽을 문간에 내린다.\n잘린 자리가 이빨 자국 없이 매끈:
Kranya drops half a deer at the door.
The cut is smooth. No tooth marks.
창 한 번에 쓰러뜨렸어!\n근데 칼 가지러 간 사이에\n뒷다리 쪽 반이:
One spear and it went down!
But while I went for my knife,
the hind half vanished.
I saw. It was dragged off.
There were no footprints.
…A shadow walked it away.
그, 그림자? 하! 그림자가 뭘 먹어?\n…먹어? 진짜로?:
A-a shadow? Hah! What would it eat?
…Eat? Truly?
오크 사냥꾼 법에 그런 게 있어.\n'뺏긴 사냥은 입 밖에 내지 마라.':
Orc hunters have a law for that.
'Speak not of a stolen kill.'
…I'm breaking it right now.
The hunter who came to boast
keeps glancing at the woods today.
Half is still a big deer.
…I know you're comforting me.
I like it anyway. Say it again.
I'll keep the broken law secret.
…Thanks. You're a bit of an orc.
대신 반쪽은 네 솥에 넣어.\n입막음 값이야. 하!:
In return, the half goes in your pot.
The price of silence. Hah!
Next time I wear my knife first.
…And I look behind me. Twice.
울타리 앞에서 끊긴 자국: Tracks That End at the Fence
Half a deer cooked well in the pot?
…But I kept thinking about it.
You didn't tell about the law? Thanks.
…But I kept thinking about it.
I followed that smooth trail.
Three nights. Three javelins.
The trail stopped dead
at this house's fence.
…It could go no further.
A thin frost sits on every fence post.
It does not melt, even at noon.
The fence kept it out.
What it kept out,
I choose not to say.
나 처음으로 아무것도 안 잡고 왔어.\n자랑할 게 없어.\n…이상하게 배:
First time I come back with nothing.
Nothing to boast of.
…Strangely, I'm not hungry either.
You can boast about the fence.
하! 울타리 자랑?\n…좋아. '그 집 울타리는\n내가 못 잡은 걸 막았:
Hah! Boast of a fence?
…Fine. 'That house's fence
stopped what I couldn't catch.'
An orc hunter boasting of a fence.
…A first. Not bad, though.
…하. 오크 집에선\n빈손으로 온 놈한테 먼저 퍼 줘.\n너, 그거 어디:
…Hah. In an orc home,
the one who comes empty eats first.
Where did you learn that?
Tomorrow I catch three rabbits.
…Not five. Three is enough.
문은 대답 안 한다 했지?\n하하, 맞았어. 오늘도 안 했어.\n…근데:
I said doors don't answer, yes?
Haha, right. Not today either.
…But the forest answered!
'괜찮다' 한마디 바란다 했지.\n그 말 들으러 또 왔는데\n…숲이 먼저:
I wanted just one 'It's alright.'
I came back to hear it, but
…the forest answered first!
Moga opens his huge palm.
A nail-sized sprout, soil and all.
지난봄 벤 참나무 그루터기에서\n이게 났어. 하하!\n용서받은 거지? 그:
It grew from the oak stump
I felled last spring. Haha!
That means I'm forgiven? Right?
…But I'm worried.
I dug it up to show you.
What if I broke its roots?
…You dug up the sprout, big fellow?
Carry forgiveness about
and it withers.
Haha… is, is that so?
…Sorry. Sorry, little sprout.
One more thing to apologize to.
The size of a fingernail.
화분! 하하! 집이 생겼네!: A pot! Haha! It has a home!
…창가면 주인 집이잖아.\n그럼 주인이 용서해 주는 거야?:
…The window is the innkeeper's house.
So the innkeeper forgives me?
…Yes. Beside its stump is right.
Haha, brought it, now bring it home.
Another thing he owes
the trees an apology for.
No axe today.
Haha! My hands hold something small.
The window sprout has two leaves!
Haha! I checked the window first.
새싹, 그루터기 옆에 데려다줬어.\n가 보니 하나 더 났더라! 하하!:
I took the sprout back to its stump.
There was another one! Haha!
…So now I think I can say it.
Why I apologize to doors.
Moga perches on the chair's edge.
It creaks. He flinches.
젊을 때, 폭풍 치던 밤에\n인간 마을 집에서 우는 소릴 들었어.\n두드:
When I was young, on a stormy night,
I heard crying in a human house.
I knocked… it didn't open.
So I pushed. Gently.
…The whole door came off.
지붕이 새서 아이가 울고 있었어.\n근데 나를 보고 더 크게 울었어.\n:
The roof leaked; a child was crying.
Seeing me, it cried louder.
…I'd been chopping wood. Axe in hand.
사과도 못 하고 나왔어.\n그 뒤로 문만 보면 말해.\n'미안하다, 고맙:
I left without saying sorry.
Since then, at every door I say,
'Sorry. Thank you.'
The apologies to doors
were the one owed to that door.
That house's door heard you too.
…그럴까? 문은 다 나무니까.\n숲 뿌리로 이어져 있으면…:
…You think? Doors are all wood.
If they join through the roots…
Haha! Then I said it a hundred times.
…I feel lighter. Truly.
This lodge's door says it's alright.
…하하. 하하하.\n주인, 지금 문 대신 말한 거지?:
…Haha. Hahaha.
Innkeeper, you spoke for the door, yes?
…Thank you.
No, thank the door too.
내일은 문을 살살 열게.\n…그래도 미리 말해 둘게.\n미안하다! 하하!:
Tomorrow I'll open the door gently.
…Still, I'll say it now.
Sorry! Haha!
지난번 재, 조금 가져갔어요.\n의식에 썼어요. 잘 됐어요.\n…하나만:
I took a little of your ash.
I used it in a rite. It went well.
…All but one thing.
스승 얘기, 들어 주셨죠.\n그 뒤로 숲 안쪽에 가 봤어요.\n…이걸 주:
You listened about my master.
After that I went deep in the forest.
…I found this.
Shaga unwraps a cloth.
A finger-long root, black as charcoal.
I rubbed this lodge's ash on it,
but the black won't go.
It's where my master's staff stood.
Only the staff… my master was gone.
북쪽 샘과 같은 빛입니다.\n뿌리는 물을 마시니까요.\n…견습 주술사,:
The same light as the north spring.
Roots drink water, after all.
…Apprentice, throw that away.
…I can't.
It's the last root
my master tried to save.
The quiet child today
clutches the cloth and won't let go.
Let me look at that root.
스승이 그랬어요. '모르는 건\n마녀한테 물어라. 값은 내고.'\n…값은:
My master said, 'What you don't know,
ask a witch. And pay her.'
…I'll pay by sweeping the ash.
…Yes. My master has never been lost.
The way back is just long.
Tonight I'll sleep by the hearth too.
…With my master's staff.
봐 주신 뿌리, 화로 옆에 뒀더니\n끝이 갈색이 됐어요.\n…아주 조금요:
The root you looked at, by the hearth,
its tip has turned brown.
…Just a little.
길을 아는 분이라 하셨죠.\n그 말, 밤마다 따라 했어요.\n재를 뿌리면:
You said my master knows the way.
I've said it every night since.
While scattering ash.
그래서 정했어요.\n스승 없이 뿌리 의식을 해 볼래요.\n처음으로, 혼자:
So I've decided.
I'll do the root rite without Master.
For the first time. Alone.
견습은 혼자 의식하면 안 돼요.\n이름을 못 받았으니까요.\n…근데 기다:
Apprentices mustn't do rites alone.
We haven't got our names.
…But if I wait, the forest dies first.
애야, 견습이 혼자 의식을 하면\n뼈가 웃는다. …나도 그랬다.\n스승:
Child, when an apprentice works alone,
the bones laugh. …So did I.
The bones named me, not my master.
…뼈가요? 할머니,\n제 몫도 던져 주실 수 있어요?:
…The bones? Grandmother,
could you cast for me too?
The casting is mine to do.
The name is yours to pick up, child.
Shaga grips ash, then opens her hand.
Ash stays in the lines of her palm.
The hand that waited for its master
now takes up the ash itself.
…With a witch as witness,
my master can't say a word.
When my master comes back, I'll say,
'The witch of the north saw it.'
Take as much ash as you need.
…Clean ash.
With this lodge's ash, even if I err,
I don't think the forest will rage.
I'll pay by sweeping ash. For life.
When the rite is done I'll come back.
…Maybe with a name.
'아직'이라 했지.\n그 뒤로 매일 던졌다.\n…뼈가 아직도 '아직'이란:
You said 'not yet.'
I've cast every day since.
…The bones still say 'not yet.'
점은 소문이라 했지, 애야.\n부락 젊은 것들도 그러더라.\n'할멈 뼈는:
You called fortunes rumor, child.
The tribe's young ones say so too.
'The crone's bones are market gossip.'
Ulma sets four bones on the table.
One has a fine crack.
오늘 아침 던졌더니\n북쪽 뼈에 금이 갔다.\n…뼈가 늙은 건지, 북쪽이:
I cast this morning
and the north bone cracked.
…Is the bone old, or the north?
어젯밤 북쪽 등불은 괜찮았어요.\n흔들린 건 다른 쪽이에요.\n…올빼미는:
The north lamp was fine last night.
It was another that wavered.
…Owls are never wrong.
하! 새가 뼈보다 빠르구나.\n그럼 이 금은 내 손이 늙은 거다.\n…그:
Hah! The bird is quicker than bone.
Then the crack is my old hand.
…That frightens me more, child.
She looks longer at the back
of her hand than at the cracked bone.
Throw it? Child, bones aren't thrown.
…They are buried.
Yes, let's bury it. Under your snow.
We'll see what it says in spring.
Use it till you find a new one.
Hah! Telling me to be thrifty?
A witch more frugal than an orc.
…A cracked bone speaks only half.
Some days half is enough to hear.
Sleep, child.
Tonight I keep watch, not the bones.
Child. I've something to leave you.
뼈를 물려줄 손: The Hand to Inherit the Bones
The bone we buried.
I looked at the yard on my way.
…The snow melted just there.
금 간 뼈, 아직 쓴다.\n네 말대로 반만 말하더라.\n…반만 들으니 편:
I still use the cracked bone.
As you said, it speaks only half.
…Hearing half is restful.
나는 곧 뼈를 못 던진다.\n손이 떨려. 뼈가 내 손을\n먼저 읽어 버린:
Soon I can't cast the bones.
My hands shake. The bones read
my hands before I read them.
부락 젊은 것들은 안 배운다.\n뼈보다 장터 소문이 빠르다고.\n…틀린:
The tribe's young ones won't learn.
Market gossip is quicker than bone.
…Not wrong, either.
할머니, 그 점술 말이오.\n내가 받아 적을 수는 있소.\n…책으로 내진:
Grandmother, about your bone-reading.
I could write it down.
…Not for a book, mind you.
Hah! Bones on paper?
…You can't cast paper, chronicler.
Ulma pushes one bone
toward the witch. An uncracked one.
One who reads what lies ahead
seeks where to leave what's after.
…Aye. No use to a witch.
You build your own days ahead.
Then it goes to a tribe child.
…The most unruly one.
I'll only keep it for you.
Only keep. Aye, that's right.
Not an owner. A keeper.
If someone comes asking for this bone
…that child is the one after me.
Sleep, child.
No bones tonight.
…I'm a little curious about tomorrow.
그때도 마녀가 있었다 했지.\n그 말을 매듭에 묶었소.\n조상 끈에 새:
You said there was a witch then too.
I tied that word into a knot.
A new knot on the ancestors' cord.
같은 불 옆에서 잤소.\n…꿈은 안 꿨소. 푹 잤지.\n조상한테 미안할:
I slept by the same fire.
…Had no dreams. Slept deep.
The ancestors would be ashamed.
Bardu unwinds a thick coil of cord.
It holds well over a hundred knots.
순례 끈이오. 걸은 곳마다 매듭.\n여기까지가 아버지 매듭이오.\n…아버:
A pilgrim's cord. A knot per place.
Up to here are my father's knots.
…Father turned back at this house.
He fell sick, they say.
Collapsed on the road home.
Only the cord came to me.
숲의 돌에 절했다고 했소?\n잘했소. 그 돌은 조상보다 늙었지.\n…절:
You bowed to the forest stone?
Well done. It's older than ancestors.
…It's earned the bow.
A dwarf praising an orc's bow.
…I'll tie it in. It's rare.
Where the father's knots stop,
the son's fingers stop too.
…아버지가 못 간 길이오.\n내가 가면 아버지 길이 되나,\n내 길이 되:
…A road my father couldn't walk.
If I walk it, is it his road,
or mine?
…I see. Beside my father's knot,
my knot. From the same house.
Father and son side by side.
…A first on the ancestors' cord.
Tonight I sleep holding Father's knot.
…The cord is warm. From the fire.
I went past my father's knots.
Three days. Snow buried the road.
…I came back. Here.
아버지 옆에 매듭을 묶고\n끈을 처음부터 다시 셌소.\n…못 읽던 매듭이:
I tied my knot beside Father's
and counted the cord from the start.
…There were knots I couldn't read.
맨 앞, 제일 오래된 매듭 둘이오.\n하나는 '받지 않은 불'.\n하나는:
At the very front, the oldest two.
One: 'The fire not taken.'
One: 'The house of the north lamp.'
같은 밤에 묶였소.\n횃불을 거절한 조상이\n그 밤에 여기까지 걸었다는:
Tied the same night.
The ancestor who refused the torch
walked all the way here that night.
…Why he walked, the cord doesn't say.
Orc knots can't tie a 'why.'
하암… 이 집 벽이 꾸는 꿈에\n문을 세게 두드리는 오크가 있어요.\n눈:
Yawn… in the dreams this house's walls
dream, an orc pounds on the door.
It was a night of heavy snow.
…꿈 기록가.\n그 오크, 숨이 찼소?:
…Dream chronicler.
Was that orc short of breath?
Bardu rubs two knots
with his thumb for a long time.
That night, whose warning did
my grandmother's grandmother hear?
He came to warn her, then.
…A warning. Then the ancestors
did more than keep the law.
They went one step further.
I'll say so to the tribe.
…With a 'perhaps' attached.
Don't ask what isn't on the cord.
…I see. What the knots didn't tie,
the ancestors chose not to tie.
I'll leave one untied as well.
How this fire felt tonight.
The pilgrimage never ends.
But this house is now
a place to return to.
솥 얘기 또 해요!: Let's talk about the pot again!
추가 요금 냈잖아요! 기억하죠?\n그날 솥, 바닥까지 긁었어요.\n…근데:
I paid the extra! Remember?
Scraped that pot to the bottom.
…But it keeps nagging me.
손님들이 착하다고 했죠?\n착한 게 아니었어요.\n…배고픈 거였어요. 다:
You said the guests were kind?
They weren't kind.
…They were hungry. All of them.
고기 낸 손님만 고기 먹고\n옆자리는 감자 먹고.\n…오크 솥은 그렇게:
Whoever paid for meat ate meat,
the next seat ate potatoes.
…An orc pot isn't run like that.
Eshka unslings her pack.
Out comes a salted pork leg.
제가 들고 온 고기예요!\n한 솥에 다 넣고 오늘 묵는 사람\n다 먹어요:
This is meat I brought!
All in one pot, and everyone staying
tonight eats. Free!
브로크 아저씨 오는 날이죠?\n후추 있으면 한 줌만 사요.\n…제 돈으로:
Brock comes today, doesn't he?
If he has pepper, I'll buy a fistful.
…With my own coin!
히익! 그, 그 솥…\n고블린은 몇 마리 들어가요?:
Eek! Th-that pot…
How many goblins fit in it?
들어가긴 뭘 들어가요!\n고블린은 먹는 쪽이에요. 앉아요!\n국자 제일:
Nobody's going in! Goblins
are the ones eating. Sit down!
You get the biggest ladle.
Meat costs extra; that's lodge law.
She strikes it head-on with a ladle.
그쵸! 제 고기, 제 솥, 제 마음!\n…규칙은 안 어긴 거예요. 그쵸?:
Right! My meat, my pot, my call!
…I didn't break the rule. Right?
I'll ladle a bowl for you, Witch.
If you don't eat, the ladle… no.
Rules are rules. Take the coin.
…알았어요. 동전은 받고\n그 동전으로 내일 고기 사 와요.\n결국 솥으:
…Fine. I take the coin
and buy meat with it tomorrow.
It all comes back to the pot. Hah!
오늘은 다 같이 먹어요.\n남기면 내일 아침 수프 돼요!:
Today we all eat together.
Leftovers are tomorrow's soup!
That free pot, everyone had two bowls.
…Except one person.
그 동전으로 고기 사 왔어요.\n솥이 한 바퀴 돌았죠.\n…근데 한 사람:
I bought meat with that coin.
The pot came full circle.
…But one person didn't eat.
You, Witch.
You always eat last.
What's gone cold. I've seen it.
Eshka holds out a ladle.
Finger marks are worn into its handle.
할머니 국자예요. 부락 요리사였죠.\n흉년 겨울에 마지막 그릇을 남 주고:
Grandma's. She cooked for the tribe.
One lean winter she gave away the last
bowl… and didn't see spring.
그래서 오크 요리사 법이 생겼어요.\n'솥 잡은 사람도 먹는다.'\n…마:
So orc cooks made a law.
'The one at the pot eats too.'
…You're at the pot too, Witch.
그 애 차는 늘 식어 있다.\n내가 백 번은 데웠지.\n…요리사 말 들어:
That child's tea is always cold.
I've warmed it a hundred times.
…Mind the cook, dear.
Thanks for taking my side, Granny!
…Both of you, sit. First bowls coming.
The first bowl is set before me.
Steam rises. When was this last?
…Hehe. Granny, did you see?
The north witch ate the first bowl.
…맛있죠? 맛있다고 해요.\n아니면 국자로… 아니에요!:
…Good, isn't it? Say it's good.
Or the ladle… no, never mind!
Let's eat together. All of us.
All together! That's the best law.
Better than Grandmother's. Shh.
…How many spoons was it?
I'll stop counting. Plenty.
이 국자, 여기 걸어 둬도 돼요?\n…다음에 올 때까지만요.\n할머니도:
May I hang this ladle here?
…Only till I come next.
Grandmother would like it here.
I sent the reply.
…Today I came by the front door.
The tusk hangs fine beside the bone.
It rattles. …A good sound.
I am back.
The door has never opened yet.
Not tonight either.
Three rabbits! Exactly three!
…For the empty-handed bowl.
오면서 울타리부터 봤어.\n아직 서리 앉아 있더라. 좋아!:
I checked the fence on the way in.
Still frosted. Good!
A whole deer this time!
Knife first. Looked back twice.
하하! 문아, 안녕!\n…오늘은 사과 안 해도 되지?:
Haha! Hello, door!
…No sorry needed today, right?
I came to see the window sprout!
Haha! It grows better than me.
또 왔다, 하하!\n…'괜찮다'는 아직 유효하지?:
Back again, haha!
…'It's alright' still holds, yes?
The rite went well.
…No name yet. Even so.
I came to sweep the ash.
It's a promise. For life.
스승 소식은 아직이에요.\n…화로 옆, 비어 있죠?:
No word from my master yet.
…The spot by the hearth, it's free?
Is the bone I left safe, child?
…Nobody's come yet? Good.
What does the bone under the snow say?
…Not spring yet, then.
Back again.
The bones still say 'not yet.'
I have returned.
I gave the tribe the 'perhaps.'
…They all liked that word.
I came to tie one more
beside my father's knot.
The same fire.
I'll sleep deep tonight too.
첫 그릇 드셨죠, 오늘도?\n…아니면 지금 떠요!:
Had your first bowl today too?
…If not, I'm ladling it now!
또 고기 들고 왔어요!\n솥은 크게, 요금은 없이!:
Brought meat again!
Big pot, no extra charge!
국자 들고 왔어요!\n추가 요금 주머니도요!:
Brought my ladle!
And the extra-charge purse too!
